title: Coefficient one-norm bounded by tree size
statement:
Let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ Boolean variables, and for each subset $S \subseteq \{0,\dots,n-1\}$ let $\mathrm{coeffs}\,T\,(S)$ denote its recursively defined Fourier coefficient at frequency $S$. Then the total absolute mass of these coefficients is bounded by the number of leaves of $T$:
\[
\sum_{S} \abs{\mathrm{coeffs}\,T\,(S)} \;\le\; \mathrm{size}(T).
\]
hypotheses_covered: T is a decision tree on n Boolean variables (arbitrary, no side conditions)
replaced:
For every decision tree $T$,
\[
\sum_{S} \abs{\mathrm{coeffs}\,T\,S} \le T.\mathrm{size},
\]
i.e.\ the spectral $1$-norm of the coefficients is at most the number of leaves.
